proposals.expected_failure_mode: May under-capture long-memory or prolonged tail behavior, leading to sharper-than-observed post-peak declines and potential underestimation during extended elevated periods.
proposals.rationale: Anchor configuration: SEIRS with delayed_I at 2 weeks matches the hypothesized admissions lag while keeping dynamics non-fractional for maximum parsimony and stability; serves as the direct comparator to the prior best fractional spec under identical delay/obs.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Can trade stability for flexibility: may over-smooth or introduce phase distortions around sharp peaks, occasionally overshooting/undershooting if memory compensates for timing mismatch.
proposals.rationale: Matched pair to isolate the effect of fractional dynamics at the same (anchor) 2-week delay; fractional memory may better accommodate high peakiness with smoother persistence without changing observation timing.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If true lag is nearer 2 weeks, may shift forecasts earlier (phase lead), producing premature peak timing and misaligned rise/decline segments.
proposals.rationale: Shorter-lag sensitivity check around the 2-week anchor while keeping non-fractional dynamics; tests whether admissions are closer to I-proxy with reduced phase shift, potentially improving peak alignment.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Risk of confounding timing and memory: may fit rise/peak well but degrade rolling stability, with inconsistent peak height due to extra flexibility.
proposals.rationale: Matched fractional/non-fractional pair at delay=1 to separate timing vs memory effects; fractional dynamics may compensate for residual lag mismatch while preserving the shorter observation delay.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Known delay sensitivity: may induce phase lag (late peaks) and amplify errors around sharp changes, especially in high-peakiness series.
proposals.rationale: Longer-lag sensitivity check around the 2-week anchor with non-fractional dynamics; evaluates robustness to potential longer admissions delay without adding compartments.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: Highest risk of instability/over-flexibility: longer delay plus fractional memory can overfit idiosyncratic segments, causing rolling-split variability and peak timing drift.
proposals.rationale: Matched pair at delay=3 to isolate fractional effect under the most timing-shifted option; tests whether memory helps stabilize forecasts when observation delay is longer.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: If hospitalization truly lags infections, this will systematically lead the target (phase lead), misplacing peaks and degrading calibration during rapid transitions.
proposals.rationale: Minimal baseline comparator without delay: tests whether explicit lag is necessary at all for this series when using the simplest SEIRS observation mapping; paired with fractional toggle only.

proposals.expected_failure_mode: May partially mimic lag via smoothing but still mis-time peaks; can also over-smooth sharp changes, reducing peak amplitude fidelity in high-peakiness periods.
proposals.rationale: Baseline fractional comparator without delay to disentangle whether fractional memory alone can mimic the effective lag/persistence seen in hospitalization rates without an explicit delay.
